title: Critical AI Literacies Through Design Justice: Redesigning Language Education
content: Taking Buzato and Gonsales’s (2025) multidimensional account of Critical AI Literacies as a point of departure, this theoretical essay asks how Design Justice can foreground the distributional conditions of AI-mediated language education. The discussion relates three uses of design without treating them as equivalent: design as semiotic transformation in multiliteracies; designs for and in learning as the organization and reworking of pedagogical conditions; and Design Justice as a political orientation to authority, participation, impacts, and alternatives. Concerns distributed across the ten Design Justice principles are grouped according to thematic convergence, conceptual proximity, and relevance to educational arrangements. This synthesis yields five interdependent dimensions: knowledge and capability; recognition and participation; power and control; impact and accountability; and alternatives and redesign. Situated within a multidimensional understanding of Critical AI Literacies, the model examines how linguistic and semiotic practices, access to knowledge, decision-making, consequences, and possibilities for change are distributed across designs for learning and designs in learning. The proposal remains conceptual and is open to implementation, empirical scrutiny, and redesign in language education.
